FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 111
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator Chris Elliott
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 03/10/2026
Senate Bill 111as introduced could, for fiscal years 2028 through 2032, decrease income tax
and utility tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund, insurance premium tax receipts to the State
General Fund, and financial institutions excise tax receipts to the State General Fund, counties,
and municipalities by a cumulative maximum of $25 million annually by allowing taxpayers to
claim a non-refundable, non-transferable tax credit, beginning in tax year 2027, up to the annual
amounts listed below for donations to certain public or private trade schools, trade programs, or
community development foundations pursuant to the provisions of this bill. This bill would
allow the credits to be carried forward up to three-years.
Taxpayer Maximum Annual Tax Credit Amount
Single, Head of Household, Married Filing
$15,000
Separately
Married Filing Jointly $30,000
Pass-Through Entity, Limited Liability
$450,000
Corporation, Professional Corporation
Subchapter C corporation Lessor of $500,000 or corporation's tax liability
This bill would create the Prepare Alabama Investment Program, administered by a
seven-member board within the Alabama Department of Workforce (DOW), to: (1) determine
the eligibility of qualifying entities to receive donations, (2) submit the list of eligible entities to
the Department of Revenue; and (3) annually publish on DOW's website a list of entities eligible
to receive donations during the next tax year.
Additionally, this bill would increase the obligations of the DOW, to: (1) jointly report with the
board to the Legislature all donations reported, and all credits claimed and approved for the
preceding tax year; and (2) retain a company to publicize the program.

This bill would also increase the administrative obligations of the DOW and the Department of
Revenue to adopt rules pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
Finally, this bill could increase the obligations of the Legislature paid from the State General
Fund and the affected state agencies to reimburse board members by an estimated minimum of
$200 per meeting, for per diem and travel expenses.
